1: Eligibility criteria for KiwiSaver government contribution (year ended 30 June 2026)
To be eligible for the government contribution, a person must have met the following criteria:
·  Contributed to their KiwiSaver account during the period 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026
·  Been a member of a KiwiSaver scheme or a complying fund
·  Lived mainly in New Zealand, or been:
·  A government employee serving overseas, or
·  Working overseas as a volunteer or for token payment for an approved charitable organisation.
·  Annual taxable income of $180,000 or less
2: The maximum government contribution for the year ending 30 June 2026 was $260.72
3: To receive the full government contribution, a person must have contributed at least $1,042.86 of their own money to their KiwiSaver account during the year.
4: If a person contributed less than $1,042.86, the government still contributed 25 cents for every dollar they contributed.
5: KiwiSaver providers claim the government contribution from Inland Revenue after 30 June each year, and it is typically deposited into members’ accounts by late July or August.
6. Member age is calculated as at 30 June 2026.

2: From 1 April 2026, the minimum employee contribution rate is 3.5% (this is also the default rate) of their gross salary or wages.

·  members can also opt for the 4%, 6%, 8% or 10% rate.

3: The contribution rate is calculated from each member's most recent payday during the year ending 30 June. If the member did not contribute through PAYE during the year they will appear as 'no contribution' in this table, even if they contributed outside of the PAYE system.
